title: reserve-vs-payg-mix-simulations
content:
Quick sim notes: payg vs reserve mix (personal scratchpad)

Context / goal:
- Need a simple model to decide what % of revenue should be captured as reserved contracts vs PAYG for H1 2025 growth plan.
- Focus on unit economics at token-level for gen calls (chat) + small embeddings traffic.
- Keep it intentionally rough — want order-of-magnitude sensitivity and a few candidate bundles.

Assumptions (baseline)
- avg gen token length per call (response only): 100 tokens
- tokens per prompt (user+system): 40 tokens
- total tokens per request = 140 tokens
- avg requests per MAU (monthly active user doing LLM ops) = 120 requests/month (≈4/day)
- tokens per MAU/month = 140 * 120 = 16,800 tokens ≈ 17k

Costs (infra)
- marginal inference cost per 1k tokens (hosted) = $0.006 per 1k tokens (baseline) -> $0.000006 per token (this is purely infra GPU amortized + infra ops)
- embedding cost per 1k dims call = $0.012 per 1k tokens equivalent (if mixing embeddings, treat separately)
- overhead (storage, tracing, billing, SRE) add ~25% on top of infra marginal -> blended marginal = 1.25 * infra
- blended marginal per token = $0.0000075 (rounded)

Revenue and price points
- PAYG list price (example candidate) = $0.00003 per token (5x blended marginal) -> gross margin per token = 0.0000225 (~75%)
- Reserved (committed monthly) blended discount candidate = 40% off PAYG -> reserved price per token = $0.000018 per token (margin ≈ 58%)
- Enterprise reserved + SLA premium: $0.000022 per token (lower discount but SLA/guarantee revenue)

Simple unit-econ per MAU (monthly)
- PAYG revenue per MAU = 17k tokens * $0.00003 = $0.51/mo
- PAYG cost per MAU = 17k * $0.0000075 = $0.1275 -> contribution = $0.3825
- Reserved revenue per MAU (if they commit same usage) = 17k * $0.000018 = $0.306 -> cost = same 0.1275 -> contribution = $0.1785

Observation: PAYG contribution per MAU > reserved contribution per MAU because reserved has discount but provides predictability. But reserved gives committed ARR and lower churn. Need to model churn sensitivity.

Scenario: convert 25% of PAYG usage to reserved contracts (mix)
- Suppose 10k MAUs total
- Baseline all PAYG revenue = 10k * $0.51 = $5,100/mo -> $61.2k/yr
- If 25% (2.5k MAU) convert to reserved -> reserved rev = 2.5k * $0.306 = $765/mo, PAYG rev from remaining 7.5k = 7.5k * $0.51 = $3,825/mo -> combined = $4,590/mo -> down from $5,100 -> delta -$510/mo but predictability increases and gross margin mix shifts slightly
- Contribution: PAYG contribution 7.5k * 0.3825 = $2,869, reserved contribution 2.5k * 0.1785 = $446.25 -> total contribution = $3,315.25 vs all PAYG contribution = $3,825 -> drop in contribution of ~$510 -> same as revenue drop above

Why still a win? (qualitative)
- Reserved contracts enable capacity planning, allow us to schedule cheaper long-lived instances -> actual infra cost for reserved might be lower than blended marginal used above if we change instance mix (e.g., dedicated GPUs at higher utilization). There's optional delta: reserved infra cost multiplier 0.85 (15% lower per-token cost). If we apply that: reserved cost per token = 0.000006375 * 1.25? (need consistent calc) -> effectively reserved contribution improves by ~10-15%.
- Reduces churn and acquisition costs (we avoid CAC for those seats monthly) -> if CAC payback time improves by X months this offsets margin drop.

Quick sensitivity tests (notes):
- If PAYG price is 3x marginal instead of 5x, PAYG becomes barely profitable; reserved becomes comparatively worse. Need to pick PAYG markup to both capture value and leave room for discounted reserved deals.
- If avg tokens per MAU is actually 50k (power users), reserved deals become proportionally more attractive to customers (capex predictability) and to us (volume discounts, smoother load).

Candidate small bundles / packaging ideas (rough)
1) Starter PAYG (free tier for up to 10k tokens/mo), then PAYG block pricing (first 1M tokens at $0.000035, next at $0.000025) -> gives price anchoring and volume incentive
2) Micro-reserved monthly packs: buy X tokens/month at 40% off PAYG; X tiers {50M, 200M, 1B} with rollover of unused tokens for 1 month. Simpler than seat+rate.
3) Session-bundle: small upfront for 30-day session credits (targeting RAG apps with stable usage). Unclear how to meter across short vs long LLM sessions.
4) Enterprise reserved with SLA + dedicated pools + long-term commit (12/24 mo) priced with blended model (flat platform fee + per-token discounted rate).

Open questions / TODOs
- Need to run traffic histogram across customers to understand percentiles of tokens/MAU (top 5% drives what %) -> affects where to anchor tiers.
- How much lower can infra marginal actually be if we shift reserved to Dedicated pools? Talk to infra (Carlos) to get per-token cost at 70% utilization on reserved sku.
- Model churn impact: estimate CAC and churn improvement for reserved (conservative: churn drop from 7% -> 4% monthly). Run NPV for 12/24 mo horizon.
- Consider non-linear discounts: larger reserved should have steeper discounts but also require minimum commit ARR. Need to simulate elastic demand.

Quick mental experiments (numbers to sanity check)
- If we set PAYG = $0.00004/token (6.7x blended marginal) and reserved = 45% off -> reserved = $0.000022 -> reserve contribution per MAU = 17k*(.000022 - .0000075) = ~$0.246 -> now reserve starts to look more OK vs PAYG contribution of $0.51 - $0.1275 = $0.3825

Notes to self:
- Present this as a 1-slide summary: 3 bullets (tradeoff: margin vs predictability), 1 chart (revenue vs % reserved), 1 ask (infra per-token at 70% util).
- Run a quick cohort sim in sheet: columns = MAU, avg tokens/month, % convert reserved, reserved discount, infra delta, CAC impact -> compute ARR, contribution, NPV.

References / links in my head:
- similar playbook from back-infrastructure at other startups: prefer smaller monthly reserved packs for SMBs, larger multi-year for enterprise.
- Slack convo thread #pricing-rev from May had notes on anchor pricing (Maya) -> follow-up: ask Maya for her raw usage histograms.

End.

(very rough; capture before meeting with product + infra next Wed)
